newsitem.title: PERU: TV cameraman to flee Peru, citing threats.
newsitem.headline: TV cameraman to flee Peru, citing threats.

text.p: A television journalist who interviewed the leader of Peru's guerrilla hostage-takers has been forced to leave Peru after receiving anonymous threats, the Peruvian Foreign Press Association said on Friday.

Miguel Real, a correspondent for international video news service Worldwide Television News (WTN), was due to leave the country late on Friday because of "veiled threats that endanger his work as a journalist as well as his physical person," the association said in a statement.
"In recent weeks, like many other international news media, WTN has interviewed on repeated occasions the MRTA command via short-wave," the statement said.
Real, a Mexican, has interviewed the head of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement, Nestor Cerpa, via walky-talky while Cerpa was inside the Japanese ambassador's residence holding 72 hostages.

News of Real's departure followed a complaint by the Peruvian government's point-man in the hostage crisis, Domingo Palermo, that some unnamed foreign journalists were "advising" the MRTA command, the statement said.
"Palermo noted that certain members of the foreign press were advising the MRTA command in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima," it said without giving details.

Palermo's complaint, made in a meeting with association president Yves-Claude Llorca, amounted to "a clear warning that the work of international media could be restricted in covering the events at the residence," the statement said.
It called on President Alberto Fujimori's government to hand over to the proper authorities any evidence it may have on ties between foreign journalists and the MRTA.
